text:
eva: Heads-up — ap-southeast-2 is showing sustained GPU pod evictions and higher 5xx for model-serving. Looks like some customers are still resolving to the old edge hostname after the failover.
sam: Confirmed. I see increased 502/504 from the staging route that was supposed to be drained. DNS records were updated ~20m ago but we still have traffic. :thinking_face:
kai: Logs from route53 weights show we adjusted weights to 0/100 to shift traffic to eu-west right after the outage. Route53 change went through at 2067893300.
eva: Can people run a few dig checks from different regions? I suspect resolver caches are holding onto a long TTL from earlier config.
oncall-lee: From my laptop (isp: telco-xyz):

> $ dig +short app.edge.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8
> 52.23.11.77

TTL returned: 3600s. That explains it.
sam: Ugh — the previous TTL was 3600. Route53 change won't evict those caches. We need to do a mitigation that doesn't rely on downstream caches honoring TTL.
eva: Options: 1) create a new short-lived steering CNAME (e.g., app-v2.edge...) and update clients who can follow CNAMEs; 2) use HTTP-level routing for clients that hit the old IP (nginx redirect to new host); 3) attempt to prime resolvers by publishing the new name and hitting widely used resolvers.
kai: I'm already spinning up a short-lived steer record: prewarm.app.edge.redwood-inference.com -> eu-west steer target, TTL=60. Planning to update main cname to point at that steer once we see resolver priming.
marie: Is adding an HTTP redirect safe? Some clients are embedded devices that don't follow redirects well.
eva: Redirect is a fallback for capable clients, not a full fix. We should also consider weighted gradual shift with active health checks so we don't slam eu-west GPU capacity.
oncall-lee: Practical step sequence I'd run:
1) publish prewarm CNAME with TTL 60
2) hit prewarm hostname from a bunch of vantage points (cloudflare workers, gce, lambda) to prime common resolvers
3) after 10-15m, change main CNAME to point to prewarm
4) lower route53 weights to accelerate
5) monitor 5xx, GPU queue length, and billing alarms

sam: I can fire off a small distributed probe. Will run these commands from our probe cluster:

for r in 8.8.8.8 1.1.1.1 9.9.9.9; do dig +short prewarm.app.edge.redwood-inference.com @$r; done

and curl checks against the old IP to see redirect behavior.
kai: Prewarm CNAME created: prewarm.app.edge.redwood-inference.com -> steer-eu-west-01.redwood.net, TTL=60. ops-bot will announce when probes start.
ops-bot: playbook-run: resolver-priming started by kai at 2067894400. Steps automated: probe matrix + postback.
marie: Reminder: priming won't help ISPs that clamp TTLs or respect a minimum cache. We should expect ~10-20% to keep pointing to old IPs for a while.
eva: Agreed. We'll implement short-term traffic-shed on the old host: change nginx on old edge to return HTTP 421 with Retry-After and an informative header pointing to new host for clients that support it.
sam: Doing nginx change now on old-edge (canary) - config snippet:

location / {
  return 421 "moved";
  add_header Retry-After "60";
  add_header X-Recommended-Host "app.edge.redwood-inference.com";
}

I'll roll to all old-edge instances in 5m if canary looks stable.
oncall-lee: Monitoring: 5xx dropped ~30% after canary redirect, eu-west GPU queue increased by ~18%, cost burn rate up ~12% (additional warmed instances).
kai: We have extra reserved capacity in dedicated pools; autoscaler is also spinning a few spot instances in eu-west. Spot preempt risk is ok because we keep the critical capacity on reserved.
marie: Cost note — we'll file a short post-incident cost amortization for the extra GPU hours. Important for finance forecasting if cross-region failovers become frequent.
eva: After priming (we ran from 40 vantage points), route53 weight moved to 0/100, and main cname now points to prewarm. We still see some resolver holdouts in APAC ISPs.
sam: Suggest adding a short-lived backup A-record with a different IP so caches that key on whole RRset might pick up change faster. But that's messy for SSL certs.
kai: SSL cert rotation is the blocker for adding alternate A. Not worth the risk right now.
eva: For the runbook updates: add resolver priming step, include nginx redirect as a standard mitigation, and call out TTL hygiene: keep steering records at <=120s for services that may need rapid failover.
marie: Also add a cost bucket label and owners for cross-region warmups.
ops-bot: incident-note: ap-southeast-2 GPU eviction -> DNS propagation friction. Actions: created prewarm CNAME, primed resolvers, nginx redirect on old-edge, adjusted route53 weights. Open follow-ups: update runbook, TTL hygiene, post-incident cost report.
eva: Thanks team. We'll keep monitoring for the next 6 hours and then start a retro. If anyone sees persistent clients from a specific AS, ping me and we'll reach out to that provider. :white_check_mark:
